protocol.buildMode: vite build (production bundle) served by vite preview; dev server never used
protocol.pairing: per repetition both build arms run adjacently; baseline/candidate order alternates per repetition
protocol.coldWarm: repetition 0 runs each arm in a fresh browser context (cold; the browser process is shared and the per-context HTTP cache is empty); repetitions 1+ re-navigate one persistent page (warm)
protocol.wallMetric: markWallMs: performance.mark(mi:render-request) -> performance.mark(mi:stable-presented) delta paired by requestId — both builds emit these marks inside the same rAF callback where requestToPresentMs is computed; identical definition in both builds. The current arm also records the trace requestToPresentMs for continuity with Stage A.
protocol.classifierMetric: stable-frame classifyMs observed from Worker frame messages (workerTiming.classifyMs): the stable-pass classification wall as each build defines it (tiled job wall from dispatch to last band, yields subtracted). Parallelism/scheduling sit inside this column; single-threaded classifier evidence remains poc/performance/results/pr2/pr2-microbench.json.
protocol.viewDriving: planned region-select chains (plus a pan step where the target center is unreachable by region selection alone); expectations replay the application viewport math and are unit-tested against src/domain/viewport.ts; achieved viewport verified per sample (exact hook readback on the current arm, 9-digit coordinate readout on the baseline arm)
protocol.hashByteOrder: SHA-256 over row-major RGBA bytes from getImageData(0, 0, width, height) of canvas.explorer__canvas
protocol.engineLabels: chromium = branded stable Google Chrome, firefox = branded stable Firefox, both headed with DevTools closed, on the declared target hardware (the machine running this harness)
protocol.pairedIntervals: 95% BCa bootstrap on warm pairs, 10000 resamples, seed 20261015 (tools/benchmark/bca.ts): median log-ratio ln(baseline/current) for the improvement, median current−baseline difference for the regression cap
protocol.outOfScope: cancellation interactions, cache/replay/recolor distributions, and catalog shard states are out of scope
